I've been farming this land for 56 years. My father planted peanut here, and I still plant peanut. The soil is sandy, good for peanut, not so good for other things.

Last year I got about 350 kg per mu, dry peanut in shell. That is about what I always get on good years. This year I will do the same as last year because last year was not bad.

For 4.1 mu, I buy 2 bags of compound fertilizer 15-15-15, each bag 50 kg. That is 100 kg total, about 24 kg per mu. So each mu gets about 3.6 kg each of N, P, K from the compound. Peanut makes its own nitrogen from the roots — my father told me this and the dealer in town said the same — so I don't need much urea. But I add a little urea before flowering, maybe 5 kg per mu, because I am afraid the plants look yellow without it. Better to spend a few yuan more than lose yield.

For potassium, peanut likes it. I buy one small bag of potassium sulfate, maybe 10 kg per mu extra. My neighbor Old Wang does this and his peanut pods are always full.

I use the improved variety seed. Luhua 14 or whatever the dealer has — my neighbors all plant it and it grows well here. The old local seed gives smaller pods.

For water, I have my well. I water once after planting to make it sprout, once at flowering when the pegs go down, and once when pods are filling if no rain. So 3 times in a dry year, 2 in a wet year. I'll plan for 3.

For spray, peanut gets leaf spot disease and aphids. I spray 3 times — once for aphids when young, twice for leaf spot in summer. The pesticide shop sells me a mix.

I plough the field in autumn after harvest, then rotary before planting in April. This is how I always do it.
